name: Delayed coking and fluid coking
applications: petroleum coke for fuel or anodes
principle: Vacuum residue is heated quickly in a furnace to 480 to 590 °C and sent to a coke drum at about 400 °C and 25 to 30 psig, where it cracks thermally over many hours. Drums run in pairs on a semi-batch cycle of 28 to 36 hours, with one filling while the other is steamed, cooled and cut out with high-pressure water.
